### Orientation

> Keyword counts below are from Crossref records for ISSN 1468-5930, dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 462 records typed journal-article, of which 354 (77%) carry a deposited abstract (the rest are mostly book reviews, which have none). Counts are over titles plus abstracts among the 354, matched locally, so they are lower bounds; title-only counts over all 462 are given in brackets where useful. Retrieved 2026-11-23. OpenAlex `works` queries were refused that day (daily budget used up).

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Normative and conceptual vocabulary dominates: "philosoph*" in 75 of 354 (21.2%), "normative" in 42 (11.9%), "conceptual" in 19 (5.4%); "empirical" in 18 (5.1%), often in arguments about empirical claims rather than empirical studies |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Almost no method terms: "interview" 4 (1.1%), "survey/questionnaire" 4 (1.1%), "qualitative" 0, "quantitative" 0, "case study" 0 |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The aims page lists environment, health care, science, technology and media, law, economics, the family, sexuality, race, gender and education as covered areas; the topic mix above spans medical ethics, war, reproduction and political philosophy |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** the aims on Wiley's product-information page say the journal "publishes original philosophical research addressing problems of practical concern" and is "open to diverse viewpoints and methods" (snapshot 2024-10-07). The Crossref abstracts of the ten most recent records show themes such as housing policy, trust and monitoring in benefits systems, mandatory service, legitimate authority in war, apologies, a duty to vote, residential segregation, trustworthy AI, gossip, republican non-domination under existential risk, and limitarianism (e.g. DOIs 10.1002/japp.70148, 10.1002/japp.70145, 10.1002/japp.70142). The earlier pass's list of 2025 authors and a rumoured call about "DEI attacks" was not verified and is dropped.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** applied-ethics argument; political philosophy; normative and conceptual analysis; philosophy of language, epistemology and philosophy of mind applied to practical questions (aims page); book reviews that engage critically with a book.

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

- Stated openness: the journal is "open to diverse viewpoints and methods" and lists "sexuality, race, gender" among its areas (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/productinformation.html, Wayback snapshot 2024-10-07); it signs the Barcelona Principles for a Globally Inclusive Philosophy (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/forauthors.html, snapshot 2024-09-26). No political or epistemological stance is stated.
- Terms in titles/abstracts, 354 records with abstracts 2021-2026 (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23): "egalitarian" 21 (5.9%), "virtue|Aristot*" 13 (3.7%), "utilitarian|consequentialis*" 8 (2.3%), "pragmati*" 8 (2.3%, mostly the ordinary word), "feminis*" 5 (1.4%), "Kant" 4 (1.1%), "Rawls*" 4 (1.1%), "libertarian" 4 (1.1%), "contractualis*/contractarian/Scanlon" 2 (0.6%), "non-ideal" 1 (0.3%), "Marx*" 0, "phenomenolog*" 0.
- Political-theory vocabulary: "democra*" 34 (9.6%), "normative" 42 (11.9%).
- OpenAlex topics (spine, 2026-07-13): Political Philosophy and Ethics 446 articles, Ethics in medical practice 239, Free Will and Agency 201.
- Reading of the counts: a normative-ethics and political-philosophy centre of gravity with egalitarian (including relational-egalitarian) vocabulary the most frequent named strand at 5.9%; no thinker or school above about 6%. This describes what is published, not editors' politics.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: the work must address "problems of practical concern" (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/productinformation.html, snapshot 2024-10-07); applied-philosophy framing is the scope test: the page says the journal "publishes all areas of applied philosophy, including applied ethics, political philosophy, philosophy of language, epistemology, and philosophy of mind", not all areas of philosophy (same page).
- Anonymity is a formal requirement: remove "all identifying information, including any acknowledgements, and the name of the file"; cite one's own papers in the third person (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/forauthors.html, snapshot 2024-09-26).
- Article types: original articles up to 8,000 words including notes, with a 150-200 word abstract; book reviews of about 1,200 words (same page).
- Practical-concern framing appears in the abstracts: 299 of 354 abstracts (84%) use first person while stating a thesis (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23); recent examples state the policy or moral problem first (e.g. DOI 10.1002/japp.70148 on housing discretion).
- Consequence of ignoring the rules: no desk-reject statement exists on the pages read; SciRev has 0 reviews (https://scirev.org/reviews/journal-of-applied-philosophy/).

Scoring rule (this pass's own convention): hits divided by the 354 records with abstracts; 0 gives 0, under 1% gives 1, 1-5% gives 2, over 5% gives 3. Scores of 4-5 need a cited editorial statement; none was found. Source: Crossref titles/abstracts for ISSN 1468-5930, 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23.

### Voice & Style

- Style rules (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/forauthors.html, Wayback snapshot 2024-09-26): Chicago Manual of Style, note-and-bibliography, endnotes, abstract 150-200 words, Word format only.
- Identity and pronouns: authors may use the pronouns they identify with and "they" as a gender-neutral pronoun; the journal says it does "not give undue weight to authors' fluency" (same page).
- First-person use in abstracts: 299 of 354 (84%) contain "I", "my", "we" or "our"; "we" appears in 173 (48.9%), "our" in 80 (22.6%), "my" in 33 (9.3%) (case-sensitive local match on Crossref abstracts 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23). The usual shape is a claim followed by "I argue".
- Recent openings sampled (DOIs): 10.1002/japp.70148 states the policy problem then "I develop an improved account"; 10.1002/japp.70147 opens with "The dominant view in philosophy of trust" then "I argue"; 10.1002/japp.70143 opens "This article considers"; 10.1002/japp.70137 opens by naming a buzzword; 10.1002/japp.70134 opens with a general observation about gossip.
- Many abstracts engage a named earlier author directly, e.g. a rejoinder (10.1002/japp.70143) and a reply to two authors (10.1002/japp.70136), so the journal carries discussion-style exchanges.

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

- Review model: triple-masked, editors and referees both unaware of author identity (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/forauthors.html, snapshot 2024-09-26).
- Editorial structure on Wiley's board page (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/editorialboard.html, Wayback snapshot 2024-09-26, own count): 2 editors, 1 editorial assistant, 6 associate editors, 1 reviews editor, a 5-person management committee, an 8-person international advisory board and 27 editorial board members.
- Editorial board members by affiliation country (own reading of institution names): UK 10, USA 8, Australia or New Zealand 5, other Europe 4 (Italy, Austria/Hungary, Denmark, Spain). The page gives no discipline labels, so disciplinary mix is not counted; all listed are philosophers' university or research-institute affiliations.
- The Society page (https://www.appliedphil.org/journal-of-applied-philosophy/, snapshot 2026-05-20) says the editors work with "six Associate Editors and an International Advisory Board"; it matches the associate-editor count above.
- OpenAlex topic mix (spine, 2026-07-13): Political Philosophy and Ethics 446, Ethics in medical practice 239.
- Reviewer behaviour itself (tone, turnaround, expectations) is not observable from public pages; SciRev has 0 reviews. The Wiley AI policy bars reviewers from uploading manuscripts to AI tools (https://www.wiley.com/en-us/publish/article/ai-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23).

### Practical Concerns

- Originality: submission implies the manuscript "has not been published, and is not under consideration, by any other journal" (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/forauthors.html, Wayback snapshot 2024-09-26).
- Anonymisation: strip identifying information from text, acknowledgements and file name; third-person self-citation (same page).
- Copyright and OA: accepted papers become the Society's copyright unless otherwise agreed; hybrid OA with CC BY, CC BY-NC or CC BY-NC-ND (same page); spine APC figure USD 3,610 (Open Access table).
- Preprints and self-archiving: governed by Wiley's publisher policy (submitted version any time; accepted version after a 12-24 month embargo, 24 months standard for humanities and social science): https://authorservices.wiley.com/author-resources/Journal-Authors/licensing/self-archiving.html (snapshot 2026-02-10).
- AI: Wiley publisher policy (https://www.wiley.com/en-us/publish/article/ai-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Independent scholars: the Society's membership "is open to anyone interested in our aims, whether or not you hold a philosophical qualification" (https://www.appliedphil.org/journal-of-applied-philosophy/, snapshot 2026-05-20); the guidelines set no affiliation requirement. Language support: a third-party editing service offers a 15% discount to authors submitting to the journal, and the journal says using it does not guarantee publication (Wiley guidelines, snapshot 2024-09-26).
- Indexing listed by Wiley: Arts & Humanities Citation Index, Social Sciences Citation Index, Scopus, Philosopher's Index, PhilPapers and others (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14685930/homepage/productinformation.html, snapshot 2024-10-07).
- Ethics-approval rules, conflict-of-interest, funding and data statements: the guidelines snapshot states none of these (checked 2026-11-23); the page may be older than current practice.

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- Any identifying information in the manuscript, acknowledgements or file name: the journal is triple-masked (Peer Review table; Framing Requirements).
- More than 8,000 words including notes: the stated limit has no negotiation route (Format table).
- Work already published or under consideration elsewhere (Practical Concerns).
- A file that is not in Word format (Format table).

### Soft Tax

- Chicago note-and-bibliography style with endnotes and a 150-200 word abstract (Format, Voice & Style).
- Timeline unknown: no decision time is stated and SciRev has 0 reviews; the earlier "8-10 weeks" claim is unverified (Review Cycle Time).
- Self-archiving of the accepted version after an embargo of 12-24 months, 24 months being the stated humanities standard (Preprint Policy; publisher-level, journal-specific figure not read).
- Open access, if wanted, carries a spine-listed charge of USD 3,610 (Open Access table).

### Best Suited For

- Normative argument about a practical problem: "normative" appears in 11.9% and "philosoph*" in 21.2% of abstracts (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Political-philosophy and applied-ethics themes in the journal's top topics: Political Philosophy and Ethics 446, Ethics in medical practice 239, War, Ethics, and Justification 193 (Subject Density).
- Single-voice argumentative papers that state a thesis: first person appears in 84% of abstracts (Voice & Style).
- Replies and rejoinders to named authors: sampled abstracts include a rejoinder and a reply (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- A qualitative, quantitative or case-study research report: each term appears in 0 of 354 abstracts (Methodological Preferences); this is rarity, not a stated exclusion.
- Work with no practical-concern angle: the aims require "problems of practical concern" (Framing Requirements).
- Authors who need a predictable decision time: no figure is stated or verified (Review Cycle Time).
